answer: Social-graph distance gating resists Sybil attacks by tying voting weight to distance from trusted seeds in a public referral graph. A newcomer enters only when an established member vouches for it, and weight grows only as attestations arrive from farther-apart nodes. Each fake identity costs the attacker one real relationship: sockpuppets cluster but stay far from the vertex where trusted paths converge, so weight decays to zero. Faking closeness means planting solid timber ties across many independent communities on the horizon: as much effort as earning the reputation it counterfeits.
